{{Short description|Subgroup of GLn(k)}}
In mathematics, a '''mirabolic subgroup''' of the [[general linear group]] GL<sub>''n''</sub>(''k'') is  a subgroup consisting of automorphisms fixing a given non-zero vector in ''k''<sup>''n''</sup>. Mirabolic subgroups were introduced by {{harv|Gelfand|Kajdan|1975}}. The image of a mirabolic subgroup in the [[projective general linear group]] is a [[Borel subgroup|parabolic subgroup]] consisting of all elements fixing a given point of [[projective space]]. The word "mirabolic" is a [[portmanteau]] of  "miraculous parabolic". As an algebraic group, a mirabolic subgroup is the [[semidirect product]] of a vector space with its group of automorphisms, and such groups are called '''mirabolic groups'''. The mirabolic subgroup is used to define the [[Kirillov model]] of a representation of the general linear group. 

As an example, the group of all matrices of the form <math> \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}</math> where {{mvar|a}} is a nonzero element of the [[field (mathematics)|field]] {{mvar|k}} and {{mvar|b}} is any element of {{mvar|k}} is a mirabolic subgroup of the 2-dimensional general linear group.
